name: Ring Indoor Cam 2nd Gen (US)

radios.note: Ring's support page lists 802.11 b/g/n on 2.4 GHz.

matter.note: No Matter claim on Ring's pages, and no CSA certification listing for a Ring camera surfaced in search.

apple_home.note: Neither the Ring support page nor its Alexa help pages mention Apple Home or HomeKit.

google_home.note: No Ring page found that lists Google Home or Google Assistant for this camera. Only forum and review mentions were seen, and those are not cited.

alexa.note: Ring's support page lists Works with Alexa. Through the Ring skill you can ask an Alexa device with a screen, such as an Echo Show, to show live view.

smartthings.note: No official Ring or SmartThings page found for this model; only forum posts, which are not cited.

home_assistant.note: The official Ring integration lists Indoor Cam (2nd Gen) among its supported stick-up cams. Which camera features it exposes was not confirmed.

hubRequired.note: Connects over Wi-Fi to the Ring app; no Ring bridge is mentioned.

localControl.note: Ring does not state whether any control works without its cloud.

power.note: Plugs into an outlet; the box has a USB-A power adapter and a micro-USB cable, per Ring's regional pages.

localStorage.note: No local recording option found on the Ring pages.

subscription.note: Ring says live view works without a plan; with one, motion videos are saved for up to 180 days.

summary: Plugged into a wall outlet through its USB adapter, the Ring Indoor Cam (2nd Gen) works with Alexa via the Ring skill: ask an Echo Show for live view. Home Assistant also lists it in the official Ring integration. Live view is free, while saved motion videos, kept up to 180 days, need a Ring Protect plan. No hub is involved. Apple Home and Google Home are not confirmed.
caveats: Saved video needs a Ring Protect plan.
Apple Home and Google Home support is not confirmed by Ring.
